sbh4.2:1.1: The gross-characteristic in all these lower planes — up through the *ākiñcanyāyatana* — is, in summary, twofold:
sbh4.2:1.2: the greater-painful, non-calm abiding-quality [*vihāritā*] of the lower-and-lower planes,
sbh4.2:1.5: He investigates by the six investigation-subjects, as appropriate.
sbh4.2:1.6: For whichever plane he wishes to make dispassion toward, the calm-characteristic is the plane above it, as appropriate —
sbh4.2:1.7: up through the practice-culminating-fruit attention. Then he is 'secluded from sense-pleasures,' or at higher levels, secluded from the analogous gross-content.
sbh4.2:2.2: Sense-desire-vitarka too is twofold: association-seclusion (*saṁprayoga-viveka*) and object-seclusion (*ālambana-viveka*).
sbh4.2:2.3: 'Separated from evil unwholesome dharmas' — [these are] the secondary defilements caused by sense-desire, the unwholesome dharmas — namely: bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct;
sbh4.2:2.5: [and] quarrel, dispute, contention, controversy, deceit, fraud, cunning, lying — [these] arise.
sbh4.2:2.6: From the abandonment of these [is] 'separated from evil unwholesome dharmas': by [seeing] no fault in non-discursive, non-investigative vitarkas, [and] by stage-pertinent vitarkas and vicāras that are antidotes to sense-desire, [that are] wholesome.
sbh4.2:2.7: 'With vitarka, with vicāra' — the consummation-of-engagement attention is the seclusion-from-sense-desires that arises immediately upon it.
sbh4.2:2.8: Caused by it, conditioned by it — by which [the Blessed One] said: 'born of seclusion' — having attained the desired-and-aspired-for goal; or from seeing fault in joy.
sbh4.2:2.9: From the departure of all dauṣṭhulya, and by abundant serenity in mind-body workability, of one counting [accumulating] joy-and-pleasure successively —
sbh4.2:2.10: first from the leaving-behind of the realm of sense-desire, from right resting-on-the-object, from the binding-up of one-pointed mindfulness — the dhyāna [is reached], from the *prayoga-niṣṭhā-phala* state attained.
sbh4.2:2.11: And further, by the abundant-cultivation that produces [the result] — [he becomes] one who gains at will (*nikāma-lābhī*), one who gains without trouble (*akṛcchra-lābhī*), one who gains without difficulty (*akisara-lābhī*) — and thus by the dhyāna-attainment he passes the night [in dhyāna], also the day, as long as he wishes, up to seven days-and-nights, by which it is said 'he dwells [in dhyāna].'
sbh4.2:3.1: [At the 1st→2nd transition:] Turning the mind away from the *savitarka-savicāra* objects,
sbh4.2:3.4: in the non-distractedly-moving object, by single-dharma-character, calm, settled, the mind proceeds.
sbh4.2:3.6: Therefore: 'By the calming of *vitarka* and *vicāra*, by inward-confidence' — by the practice of *avitarka-avicāra-samādhi*, transcending the interrupted state, he attains the uninterrupted state.
sbh4.2:3.7: Therefore: 'By one-pointedness of mind' — by completely abandoning *vitarka-vicāra* in every way, the *avitarka-avicāra* practice-culminating attention is the *samādhi*. Immediately following, conditioned by it, the next arises.
sbh4.2:3.8: Therefore: 'Born from concentration' — from the attainment of the desired, blameless object, or from seeing the fault in *prīti* coming next.
sbh4.2:3.9: Pacifying gone-to-elation and gone-to-dejection, by the disappearance of all encumbrance belonging to the *vitarka-vicāra*-first-*dhyāna*-defilement side, the counter-action of which is *praśrabdhi*, the workableness of mind-and-body —
sbh4.2:3.10: 'Rapture-and-happiness' — by the same understanding as before. By progression, the second comes to be. Everything else as before.
sbh4.2:4.1: He sees the fault in the rapture-signs.
sbh4.2:4.3: At that time, he has recognized two mind-disturbing obstructions:
sbh4.2:4.4: when placing the mind in the raptureless third *dhyāna*,
sbh4.2:4.5: in the second *dhyāna* there were *vitarka-vicāra*; here it is rapture. Therefore: 'He abides in equanimity.'
sbh4.2:4.9: by which uninterrupted equanimity does not proceed.
sbh4.2:4.10: In the second *dhyāna* there is rapture,
sbh4.2:4.11: by which here too uninterrupted equanimity does not proceed.
sbh4.2:4.12: Therefore in this contemplator, in the first and second *dhyāna*s, equanimity is not yet; for which reason in the third *dhyāna* 'he abides in equanimity' is said.
sbh4.2:4.13: He, abiding in equanimity, abides thus with mindfulness established.
sbh4.2:4.15: if, due to non-cultivation of the third *dhyāna*, by lapse-of-mindfulness, occasionally perception-and-attention conjoined-with-rapture occur in the mind —
sbh4.2:4.16: those, those, lightly, lightly indeed, by wisdom he penetrates.
sbh4.2:4.18: As they arise, arise, he does not endorse them.
sbh4.2:4.20: pushes out; equanimously regards the mind.
sbh4.2:5.1: By that equanimity, by frequent practice, what is conjoined with rapture is abandoned.
sbh4.2:5.2: That mind-agitating factor [is abandoned]; raptureless, calm, fully-calmed feeling arises in the mind.
sbh4.2:5.3: By counter-action to rapture, at that time, in the form-body and the mind-body, happiness and *praśrabdhi*-happiness are experienced.
sbh4.2:5.5: that form-happiness does not exist; nor does uninterrupted equanimity. From the third *dhyāna* upward, although equanimity is found,
sbh4.2:5.7: Below, sense-pleasure-equanimity is absent; above, happiness is absent.
sbh4.2:5.8: This is that base — the third *dhyāna* — which the noble ones declare.
sbh4.2:5.9: In dependence on this, the attaining-and-abiding person who is mindful and the happy-abider attains and abides in the third *dhyāna* — so the noble ones, the elders, the elder disciples say.
sbh4.2:6.1: Because it is not of the same class,
sbh4.2:6.2: the counteragent for abandoning *sukha* is not separately stated.
sbh4.2:6.3: Only the abandoning of *sukha* brought about by that counteragent is stated.
sbh4.2:6.6: By practicing this, he drops out from the third-*dhyāna* plane where *sukha* is present, and abandons that *sukha*.
sbh4.2:6.7: Therefore: '[Damaged/Conjectural: By abandoning *sukha* and abandoning *duḥkha*], and previously by the disappearance of *saumanasya* and *daurmanasya*.'
sbh4.2:6.8: In the fourth-*dhyāna*-attainment-time, that contemplator attains the transcendence of pleasure-and-pain.
sbh4.2:6.9: Of what was previously abandoned, of what is now abandoned,
sbh4.2:6.11: 'From the abandoning of pleasure, from the abandoning of pain, from the previous disappearance of joy and dejection.'
sbh4.2:6.12: *Sukha* is not abandoned only at the time of fourth-*dhyāna* attainment: *duḥkha* [was abandoned] at the time of second-*dhyāna* attainment, *saumanasya* disappeared at the time of third-*dhyāna* attainment, and *daurmanasya* at the time of first-*dhyāna* attainment. Thus, from the abandoning of pleasure-and-pain, he has neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, but it is not yet distinctive.
sbh4.2:6.13: Therefore: 'Neither-painful-nor-pleasant' — at that time, taking the first *dhyāna* as the starting reference, all the lower-plane obstructions are abandoned.
sbh4.2:6.15: By the abandoning of these, the equanimity there arising,
sbh4.2:6.16: and the mindfulness — that becomes purified,
sbh4.2:6.17: fully clarified. By which his mind, having attained the fourth *dhyāna*, stands without movement —
sbh4.2:7.1: Of one whose mind is resolved on space, the form-perception — connected with blue-yellow-red-white etc. — is transcended by indifference-toward and dispassion-toward.
sbh4.2:7.2: Therefore: 'From the transcendence of form-perceptions' — for the cause of the mind proceeding to the limit. The obstruction-perceptions of various kinds, many-and-varied, caused by the accumulation-of-color, those go away.
sbh4.2:7.3: Therefore: 'From the disappearance of obstruction-perceptions.' Or, by the cause-of-disappearance of those, the abundance-perception proceeding in the remaining superior aggregations — namely, perceptions of food, drink, clothing, ornaments, house, garden, forest, army, mountain, etc.
sbh4.2:7.4: — in those, all and every directed-effort no longer proceeds.
sbh4.2:7.6: Having thus cultivated [release from] form-, obstruction-, and manifold-perceptions, he becomes resolved on space by the infinity-aspect.
sbh4.2:7.7: Therefore: 'Infinite space' — taking the immediate-vicinity, transcending — from the practice-culminating attention to the high-practice-culminating-fruit, he attains the basic attainment.
sbh4.2:7.8: Therefore: 'Having attained, he abides in the infinity-of-space-base.'
sbh4.2:8.1: Until the basic attainment is not attained,
sbh4.2:8.2: for the attainer of the space-as-object stage, that and the other aggregates are own-plane; the immediate-vicinity ones are also lower-plane aggregates.
sbh4.2:8.3: By a moment of consciousness, infinite space is resolved-on.
sbh4.2:8.4: That very consciousness, with the infinite-aspect of space-resolve —
sbh4.2:8.7: that very consciousness is resolved-on with the infinite-aspect.
sbh4.2:8.8: With its immediate-vicinity, the basic *ākāśānantyāyatana* is transcended.
sbh4.2:8.10: He, transcending the immediate-vicinity of *vijñānānantyāyatana*, from the practice-culminating attention to the basic-practice-culminating-fruit, attains.
sbh4.2:8.11: Therefore: 'Having attained, he abides in the *vijñānānantyāyatana*.'
sbh4.2:9.1: He, dropping out from the *vijñānānantyāyatana*, searching for an object beyond consciousness, does not find one —
sbh4.2:9.2: neither connected with form, nor formless.
sbh4.2:9.3: Not finding that object, transcending the *vijñānānantyāyatana*-with-its-immediate-vicinity, he resolves: 'There is nothing else as an object.'
sbh4.2:9.4: He becomes resolved on the perception of nothingness.
sbh4.2:9.5: By the abundance of this perception-resolve, transcending the *ākiñcanyāyatana*-immediate-vicinity, from the practice-culminating attention, he attains the basic practice-culminating-fruit.
sbh4.2:9.6: Therefore: 'Transcending the *vijñānānantyāyatana* completely, there is nothing, the *ākiñcanyāyatana* — having attained, he abides.'
sbh4.2:10.1: Therefore: 'Perceiving' — namely, dropping out from the *ākiñcanyāyatana*,
sbh4.2:10.2: gross-perceiving, fault-perceiving the perception-of-nothingness, he turns away the *ākiñcanyāyatana*-perception.
sbh4.2:10.3: By that previous *ākiñcanyāyatana*-attainment-time, the perception-of-nothingness was transcended; now the *non*-perception-of-nothingness has come to be transcended.
sbh4.2:10.4: Therefore: 'Perceiving' — [Damaged/Conjectural: neither with perception of something, nor with perception of nothingness, nor with complete non-perception]. Not, however, that all and every perception of his is ceased.
sbh4.2:10.5: As in the non-perception-attainment or the cessation-attainment — but here, a subtle perception proceeds, with sign-as-object.
sbh4.2:10.7: Thus resolved on that sphere, having transcended the *sāmantaka* and *maula* sphere of nothingness, [proceeding] from the *sāmantaka* of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception up through the *prayoganiṣṭha* attentions, he attains the *prayoganiṣṭhāphala maula*.
sbh4.2:10.8: By this he says: 'Having entirely transcended the sphere of nothingness, having attained the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he abides [in it].'
sbh4.2:10.9: There, at the time of *dhyāna-attainment*, [the sign is] as if descending downward into the underworld —
sbh4.2:10.11: At the time of *ārūpya-attainment*, [the sign is] as if falling from space.
sbh4.2:10.12: There [in both cases], right engagement [comes] from the equanimous attention at the *śamatha*-time.
sbh4.2:12.1: There are two non-conscious attainments: the non-perception attainment and the cessation attainment.
sbh4.2:12.2: The non-perception attainment is entered by an ordinary person using perception-turned-away attention; the cessation attainment, however, is entered only by a noble one.
sbh4.2:12.3: By two attentions, entry into these two attainments occurs:
sbh4.2:12.4: namely, into the non-perception attainment by perception-turned-away attention; into the cessation attainment by attention dropping-out from *naivasaṁjñā-nāsaṁjñā* and resolving-on-cessation-of-object.
sbh4.2:12.5: Now, perception is illness, perception is a boil, perception is an arrow — this is peace, this is the sublime, namely the unperceptional [attainment].
sbh4.2:12.6: Taking up an attention turned away from perception, [one] follows the non-attention to perception [as each impulse of] memory of perception arises and arises.
sbh4.2:12.7: Through cultivation, on the path of preparation, there is a state still with mind.
sbh4.2:12.8: And to one who has entered the attainment along with [its supporting] attention, mind no longer functions.
sbh4.2:12.9: Thus, by an attention preceded by the perception of escape, in one free of passion for the [Śubha-]kṛtsna [and] free of passion for the bṛhatphala [heavens], the cessation of mind and mental dharmas — this is called the unperceptional attainment.
sbh4.2:12.10: And this is how it is obtained.
sbh4.2:12.11: Then, the noble one who has gained the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, wishing to abide in a further peaceful abode, raises [his] mind out of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
sbh4.2:12.12: That mind, [thus] raised, does not find an object.
sbh4.2:12.15: Thus, for a trainee or an arhat free of passion for the sphere of nothingness, by an attention preceded by the perception of [peaceful] abiding, the cessation of mind and mental dharmas — this is called the cessation-attainment; and this is how it is obtained.
sbh4.2:13.1: By the basis of *dhyāna*, the manifestation of the five higher knowledges occurs.
sbh4.2:13.3: Just as the contemplator becomes an attainer
sbh4.2:13.5: Relying on that pure *dhyāna*: whatever dharma he has heard, grasped, fully obtained — bearing on the higher-knowledge-predominant, namely the range-of-supernormal-power, recollection-of-past-abodes, divine-ear, divine-eye, knowledge-of-others'-minds — that very dharma he attends to with concentrated-plane-attention. He becomes meaning-knower
sbh4.2:13.7: Of that meaning-knowing, dharma-knowing practitioner, shaping the mind in such-and-such ways through frequent cultivation —
sbh4.2:13.8: there comes a time and occasion when his fruits of cultivation, the five higher knowledges, arise.
sbh4.2:14.1: Moreover, the one expert in meaning and in dharma, in order to bring forth all the abhijñās, cultivates twelve saṁjñās.
sbh4.2:14.5: the perception of body-mind co-presence, the perception of resolve,
sbh4.2:14.6: the perception of recollecting past-experienced conduct in sequence,
sbh4.2:14.7: the perception of the assembled noise of various kinds of sound, the perception of luminous-form-signs,
sbh4.2:14.8: the perception of form-changes produced by defilements, the perception of resolve, the perception of the abhibhvāyatanas, and the perception of the kṛtsnāyatanas.
sbh4.2:15.1: Now, in the perception of lightness, one resolves oneself as light.
sbh4.2:15.2: As a tuft of cotton-wool, or a tuft of kapok.
sbh4.2:15.3: Or one [resolves oneself] upon a wind-disk; thus resolved, one impels [oneself] there by attention conjoined with resolve.
sbh4.2:15.4: As from couch to seat to couch —
sbh4.2:15.5: so from couch to grass-mat to couch.
sbh4.2:15.7: one resolves the body as soft.
sbh4.2:15.8: As silk-cotton, or fine cotton, or down.
sbh4.2:15.9: Thus the perception of softness nourishes and supports the perception of lightness, by which the latter — supported — comes to extension, growth, and amplitude.
sbh4.2:15.10: Then the perception of the space-element: by this perception, one resolves oneself as light and soft.
sbh4.2:15.11: If one wishes to go somewhere,
sbh4.2:15.12: one resolves the [intervening] obstructive form-spaces as [open] space, for passage through them.
sbh4.2:15.13: [All this] by an attention conjoined with resolve.
sbh4.2:15.14: Then the perception of body-mind co-presence: by which one sets the mind into the body,
sbh4.2:15.15: or the body into the mind, whereby the body becomes lighter, softer, more workable, more luminous.
sbh4.2:15.16: [The body becomes] mind-conforming, mind-bound, proceeding in dependence on mind.
sbh4.2:15.17: Then the perception of resolve: by which one resolves the distant as near, the near as distant, the small as large, the large as small, earth as water, water as earth — thus making each of the great elements interchangeable with the others.
sbh4.2:15.18: And in detail, one similarly resolves [things] as transformed, [whether] form-transformations or sound-transformations.
sbh4.2:15.19: By these five saṁjñās, perfected through cultivation, one experiences various kinds of supernatural feats — being one, manifesting [oneself as] many;
sbh4.2:15.20: namely, by the resolve-perception of creation, manifesting [oneself as] many, then becoming one again.
sbh4.2:15.21: Namely, by the resolve-perception of disappearance of the creation, one passes through walls, through ramparts, with body unhindered;
sbh4.2:15.23: one performs emerging and submerging in the earth
sbh4.2:15.24: as if in water, [or] one goes through the water with a [parted-water] current as if it were broken.
sbh4.2:15.25: Likewise one walks cross-legged on space as if on earth.
sbh4.2:15.26: Like a winged bird; or one touches with the hand even these so-mighty, so-powerful sun and moon.
sbh4.2:15.28: Up to the Brahmā world one wields the body.
sbh4.2:15.29: By the resolve-perception, taken together with the perceptions of lightness, softness, space-element, and body-mind co-presence, one accomplishes all this.
sbh4.2:15.31: Now this twofold mastery of the Brahmā-world, by body and by going, [is to be understood]
sbh4.2:15.33: Just as by resolve, or the [downward] wish to go from the Brahmā-world to beings [there], and to the form-derivative [substance] of one of them.
sbh4.2:15.34: Then the perception of recollecting past-experienced conduct in sequence: by which, from the state of childhood onward, wherever one's memory functions,
sbh4.2:15.36: wherever the noble one has gone, stood, sat, lain — recollecting in detail all past-experienced conduct in coarse sequence, without skipping, one knows it.
sbh4.2:15.37: Through cultivation, the fruit of cultivation: one recollects manifold past abodes, even back through saṁsāra, with their distinctive marks, in detail.
sbh4.2:15.38: Then the perception of the assembled noise of various kinds of sound:
sbh4.2:15.39: in a village, a town, a guild, a corporation, an assembly, a wide hall, or a chamber — the various assembled and gathered noise — mingled, varied, [a sound that] issues forth,
sbh4.2:15.41: Or the roar of a great flowing river: taking the sign there, the cultivation of perception by which, with attention based in the concentrated stage, one directs [attention] to noble and ignoble sounds, divine and human, far and near.
sbh4.2:15.42: Through cultivation, one gains the divine ear as the fruit of cultivation,
sbh4.2:15.43: by which one hears divine and human sounds,
sbh4.2:15.44: both those that are far and those that are near.
sbh4.2:15.46: as before, taking the light-sign, one attends to that very sign.
sbh4.2:15.47: This is the perception of luminous-form-signs.
sbh4.2:15.48: Through cultivation, one gains the knowledge of passing-away-and-rebirth as the fruit of cultivation,
sbh4.2:15.49: by which one sees, with the divine eye purified, beings — in detail — being reborn at the breakup of the body in good destinies, in heavenly worlds, among the gods.
sbh4.2:15.50: Then the perception of form-changes produced by defilements:
sbh4.2:15.51: by which one observes the form-state of beings stained by lust, by aversion, by delusion — beings with minds bound by anger, resentment, burning, shamelessness, unconcern, defilements, and secondary defilements —
sbh4.2:15.53: Thus is the form-state of one enraged by [some] form,
sbh4.2:15.55: namely, agitation of the senses, smiling face.
sbh4.2:15.56: Thus is the form-state of one disgusted by [some] form,
sbh4.2:15.58: namely, paleness of face, stammering voice,
sbh4.2:15.60: Thus is the form-state of one deluded,
sbh4.2:15.62: namely, muteness, failure to engage in the determination of meaning, ordinary or extraordinary speech-utterance.
sbh4.2:15.63: By these aspects of such kinds — up through one bound by shamelessness and unconcern — whatever form-state arises,
sbh4.2:15.65: taking the sign of that, one attends.
sbh4.2:15.66: Through cultivation, the knowledge of others' minds arises as the fruit of cultivation,
sbh4.2:15.67: by which one knows the applied-thought, sustained-thought, and mind of other beings and persons — mind by mind, as it actually is.
sbh4.2:15.68: Then the cultivation of perceptions of vimokṣa, abhibhvāyatana, and kṛtsnāyatana is to be understood as before.
sbh4.2:15.70: By this cultivation, one accomplishes noble supernatural power —
sbh4.2:15.71: [the power] of transforming things, of creation, of resolve.
sbh4.2:15.73: and the four *pratisaṁvids*: discrimination of dharma, discrimination of meaning, discrimination of language, and discrimination of expression.
sbh4.2:16.1: Now this is the distinction of noble supernatural power from ignoble:
sbh4.2:16.2: by noble supernatural power, whatever object one transforms,
sbh4.2:16.6: By it, in every way, the task can be accomplished.
sbh4.2:16.7: By ignoble [supernatural power], on the other hand, it does not become so; rather,
sbh4.2:16.8: as with an illusionist's display, only a mere showing is manifested.
